annotation.title_clean: Proposal for consensus recommendations in relation to the clarification, consideration and development of aspects of the normative and operational framework on emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems
annotation.title_en: Proposal for consensus recommendations in relation to the clarification, consideration and development of aspects of the normative and operational framework on emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
annotation.venue: CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (CCW/GGE.1/2021/WP.6)
named_instruments_referenced: CCW GGE Guiding Principles on LAWS
ICRC Position on Autonomous Weapon Systems 2021
annotation.summary_en: ICRC working paper submitted to the 2021 CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS. It urges States to adopt new legally binding rules: prohibit unpredictable autonomous weapons, prohibit those that target people, and regulate the others by limiting targets, duration, scope and situations of use, and by requiring human supervision.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomous weapon systems pose humanitarian, IHL-compliance and ethical risks because human control and judgement over the use of force is lost
Prohibit unpredictable autonomous weapon systems whose effects cannot be sufficiently understood, predicted and explained
Prohibit autonomous weapon systems designed or used to apply force against persons
Regulate the remaining systems by limiting target types, duration, geographic scope, scale and situations of use
Require human–machine interaction that ensures effective human supervision, timely intervention and deactivation, set through new legally binding international rules
